response.original_text: DEFENDING LOREN: ADVOCACY NOT AN ALIBI, FRIENDSHIP NOT PROOF OF INNOCENCE Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay. We had an interesting discussion with renowned law professor Atty. Tony La Viña, whom we invited for a live interview, about his decision to serve as spokesperson for Sen. Loren Legarda amid the controversies surrounding her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste. Tony began his defense of Loren by saying that he has known her from way, way back. He pointed to the senator’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes. In an earlier Facebook post, he cited Loren’s environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act and Renewable Energy Act, among others. He then used this record to argue that the allegations against Loren have “no basis.” This argument is as dim as Leandro’s solar projects. It is a non sequitur. So what if a politician has a long list of advocacies? It is not an alibi for plunder or abuse of power. A politician can champion the sun and trees, turtles, dolphins and all the animals in Noah’s Ark and still ransack the nation’s coffers. Following this logic, the large-scale corruption, extrajudicial killings and election cheating under former president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo would likewise have “no basis” because she was a pro-life advocate who lifted the death penalty. The accusations against Sen. Pia Cayetano for spreading fake news through a spliced video of Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno would similarly have “no basis” because she is a champion of reproductive health. And allegations of ghost and anomalous projects against Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano would have “no basis” because he is a devout Christian. After all, he is the “Ambassador of Jesus Christ.” But the most stupefying of Tony’s defenses of Loren and her son is his claim that they are “victims of political persecution.” Ah, yes. The same “political persecution” line now doing heavy duty in the political vocabulary of twice-impeached Vice President Sara Duterte. Please. Let us not insult those who actually suffered political persecution, such as ML Representative Leila de Lima who, as a senator, was unjustly and without any basis imprisoned by the Duterte regime for seven years. Whatever political intramurals Loren and her son may have with the administration, these do not erase, or even diminish, the serious allegations they face and the public’s legitimate demand for truth and accountability. Frankly, it would have been far more understandable and tolerable if Atty. Tony La Viña had simply said that he was choosing Loren’s side because she is a close friend. Period. Tony is free to stand by a friend, just as Loren is lucky to have a friend in him. Friendship may explain why one chooses to defend someone even if it does not prove the absence of wrongdoing. But to dress up a defense in weak arguments? Now that is something else. Advocacy does not immunize a politician from scrutiny or accountability. And friendship, however genuine, is not evidence of innocence.

DEFENDING LOREN: ADVOCACY NOT AN ALIBI, FRIENDSHIP NOT PROOF OF INNOCENCE Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay.
We had an interesting discussion with renowned law professor Atty. Tony La Viña, whom we invited for a live interview, about his decision to serve as spokesperson for Sen. Loren Legarda amid the controversies surrounding her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste.
Tony began his defense of Loren by saying that he has known her from way, way back.
He pointed to the senator’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes.
In an earlier Facebook post, he cited Loren’s environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act and Renewable Energy Act, among others.
He then used this record to argue that the allegations against Loren have “no basis.”
This argument is as dim as Leandro’s solar projects.
It is a non sequitur.
It is not an alibi for plunder or abuse of power.
A politician can champion the sun and trees, turtles, dolphins and all the animals in Noah’s Ark and still ransack the nation’s coffers.
Following this logic, the large-scale corruption, extrajudicial killings and election cheating under former president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo would likewise have “no basis” because she was a pro-life advocate who lifted the death penalty.
And allegations of ghost and anomalous projects against Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano would have “no basis” because he is a devout Christian.
After all, he is the “Ambassador of Jesus Christ.”
But the most stupefying of Tony’s defenses of Loren and her son is his claim that they are “victims of political persecution.”
The same “political persecution” line now doing heavy duty in the political vocabulary of twice-impeached Vice President Sara Duterte.
Let us not insult those who actually suffered political persecution, such as ML Representative Leila de Lima who, as a senator, was unjustly and without any basis imprisoned by the Duterte regime for seven years.
Whatever political intramurals Loren and her son may have with the administration, these do not erase, or even diminish, the serious allegations they face and the public’s legitimate demand for truth and accountability.
Tony is free to stand by a friend, just as Loren is lucky to have a friend in him.
Friendship may explain why one chooses to defend someone even if it does not prove the absence of wrongdoing.
Now that is something else.
Advocacy does not immunize a politician from scrutiny or accountability.
And friendship, however genuine, is not evidence of innocence.

claims.evidence_context:
DEFENDING LOREN: ADVOCACY NOT AN ALIBI, FRIENDSHIP NOT PROOF OF INNOCENCE Last Friday, I co-hosted TV5’s Storycon with Philippine STAR editor-in-chief Amy Pamintuan and veteran journalist Regina Lay.
We had an interesting discussion with renowned law professor Atty. Tony La Viña, whom we invited for a live interview, about his decision to serve as spokesperson for Sen. Loren Legarda amid the controversies surrounding her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste.
Tony began his defense of Loren by saying that he has known her from way, way back.
He pointed to the senator’s legislative record, particularly her years of championing environmental causes.
In an earlier Facebook post, he cited Loren’s environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act and Renewable Energy Act, among others.
He then used this record to argue that the allegations against Loren have “no basis.”
This argument is as dim as Leandro’s solar projects.
It is a non sequitur.
It is not an alibi for plunder or abuse of power.
A politician can champion the sun and trees, turtles, dolphins and all the animals in Noah’s Ark and still ransack the nation’s coffers.
Following this logic, the large-scale corruption, extrajudicial killings and election cheating under former president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo would likewise have “no basis” because she was a pro-life advocate who lifted the death penalty.
And allegations of ghost and anomalous projects against Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano would have “no basis” because he is a devout Christian.
After all, he is the “Ambassador of Jesus Christ.”
But the most stupefying of Tony’s defenses of Loren and her son is his claim that they are “victims of political persecution.”
The same “political persecution” line now doing heavy duty in the political vocabulary of twice-impeached Vice President Sara Duterte.
Let us not insult those who actually suffered political persecution, such as ML Representative Leila de Lima who, as a senator, was unjustly and without any basis imprisoned by the Duterte regime for seven years.
Whatever political intramurals Loren and her son may have with the administration, these do not erase, or even diminish, the serious allegations they face and the public’s legitimate demand for truth and accountability.
Tony is free to stand by a friend, just as Loren is lucky to have a friend in him.
Friendship may explain why one chooses to defend someone even if it does not prove the absence of wrongdoing.
Now that is something else.
Advocacy does not immunize a politician from scrutiny or accountability.
And friendship, however genuine, is not evidence of innocence.
